headlines.title: Planes, banks and the NSA all went down in one week
headlines.summary: In six days, Microsoft 365 went down, every U.S. flight was grounded, big banks showed $0 balances and the NSA's classified network went offline. Officials blame faulty servers and aging systems. Host Ejaaz Ahamadeen walks through each one, asks if it's all a coincidence and breaks down what Google and the FBI revealed about AI-run hacking.

headlines.title: Why Huang's Exit May Not Sink Nvidia Stock
headlines.summary: Nvidia has lost the only CEO it ever had. Jensen Huang co-founded the company in 1993 and ran it until he resigned. Nvidia announced the change on Thursday, Nov 12, before the market opened. Its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, became interim CEO. On Tuesday, Nov 17, the board's chair said the board does not intend to bring Huang back.

headlines.title: CME vs. Upstart: Which Financial Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
headlines.summary: CME's roughly $4 billion profit and near-zero leverage stand in contrast to Upstart's 64% revenue surge, but the lending specialist's leverage and negative free cash flow tell a different story.

headlines.title: Apple Is the Only Magnificent Seven Stock Near a Record
headlines.summary: While the S&P 500 stumbled through a fourth straight loss, one megacap barely flinched and left its six peers far behind. Its premium price, a memory cost squeeze, and a Fed minutes release could test whether this refuge holds.

headlines.title: Broadcom Plummeted 20% Over 6 Months: This Respected Tech and Hardware Research Firm is Confident 110% Returns Materialize
headlines.summary: Broadcom keeps beating earnings, yet its stock keeps sliding while the broader market climbs. One Street-high forecast defies the gloom, but a Google sourcing shift and uncapped financing guarantees could decide whether anyone should trust it.

description: Alphabet Inc. offers various products and platforms in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia-Pacific, Canada, and Latin America. It operates through Google Services, Google Cloud, and Other Bets segments. The Google Services segment provides products and services, including ads, Android, Chrome, devices, Gmail, Google Drive, Google Maps, Google Photos, Google Play, Search, and YouTube. It is also involved in the sale of apps and in-app purchases and digital content in Google Play and YouTube; and devices, as well as the provision of YouTube consumer subscription services, such as YouTube TV, YouTube Music and Premium, NFL Sunday Ticket, and Google One. The Google Cloud segment offers consumption-based fees and subscriptions for AI solutions, including AI infrastructure, Vertex AI platform, and Gemini enterprise. It also provides cybersecurity, and data and analytics services; Google Workspace that include cloud-based communication and collaboration tools for enterprises, such as Calendar, Gmail, Docs, Drive, and Meet; and other enterprise services. The Other Bets segment sells transportation and internet services. Alphabet Inc. was incorporated in 1998 and is headquartered in Mountain View, California.
